lots.what_it_is: Unknown Warrior Centenary 1920 Heritage Gold Sovereign Set, set 31 of 49: a 1920 George V gold sovereign (mint not confirmed, most likely Perth) plus a coloured 2020 UK 5 pound cupro-nickel coin, cased with certificate and booklet. Private marketing set, not a Royal Mint product.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 3 certificate reads 'Limited to just 49 sets of which this is set number 31', signed Linda MacLennan, General Manager. Photo 4: date 1920, B.P. initials right of the date; enlarged crop of the ground line (where the mint letter sits on 1920 sovereigns) shows no clear M, P or S, but the photo is only 450 x 600 px so this is not conclusive. London struck no sovereigns in 1920, so the coin must be from Melbourne, Perth or Sydney (a 1920 Sydney is a major rarity; Perth is by far the most common). Photo 5 obverse George V bare head, crisp, light wear on high points. Photos 6-7: 2020 5 pound, 'Lest We Forget', coloured poppy field, IRB obverse, capsuled. Box, plaque and booklet present.
lots.condition: Sovereign lightly circulated to about EF, no visible damage or mounting marks; box and papers appear complete. Weight and mint letter not confirmed.

The 5 pound coin asks AUD 28-32. Nothing found for the set itself. Melt check: a sovereign holds 0.2354 oz fine gold, x AUD 5,998.29/oz (Downies live spot, 30 Sep 2026) = about AUD 1,412, which is above all the 2024-25 sales because gold has risen since. GBP at 1.8929.
lots.working: Keep: lowest same-item SOLD = Lugosi AUD 800 (Feb 2025); 800 / 1.198 = 667.8, round down = 665. Flip: likely resale from SOLD evidence AUD 800, less 12% selling fees (AUD 96) and AUD 15 tracked postage = 689; 689 / 2.396 = 287.6, round down = 285. Big caveat: the current Gowans bid is already AUD 1,000, above both figures. The rule-based numbers rest on a sale made when gold was far cheaper; the coin's gold alone is worth about AUD 1,412 at today's spot, so hammer AUD 1,175 (AUD 1,408 all-in) is roughly break-even on melt. Going above 665 is a judgement call on the gold price, not something the SOLD evidence supports.
lots.confidence_reason: Set and date clearly read and two same or close SOLD results opened, but the mint letter is unread (Perth assumed; Melbourne or Sydney would only add value), the best sale is 19 months old at a much lower gold price, and the set itself has no public sales.
lots.question_for_gowans: Please confirm the mint letter on the ground line above the date of the sovereign (M, P or S), the coin's weight (should be about 7.99 g), whether it can be removed from the capsule for inspection, and that the booklet and outer box are complete.

lots.what_it_is: Nyakul Dawson (c.1930s-2007, Irrunytju/Wingellina), acrylic on linen dot painting, 2003, Irrunytju Arts cat. no. IRRND03005 on the turnover, 81.5 x 119.8 cm per Gowans, stretched, unframed.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 3: turnover inscribed 'IRRND03005 - Nyakul Dawson - Irrunytju 2003', matching the Irrunytju Arts cat. number format (IRRND + year + number) seen on his auction records. Photos 1-2: red concentric roundels and meandering bands outlined in white dots, green and yellow infill on black; typical of his 2003-04 work. Photo 4: stretcher with cross bar and hanging wire, a few paint flecks and marks on the back of the canvas, no art centre certificate, label or gallery sticker visible. Size taken from the Gowans description, not measurable in photos.
lots.condition: Front looks clean with no visible losses in the two front photos; back shows minor marks and a white smear on the cross bar. Edges and corners not fully visible.
